version: Flutter 3.47.8 (framework 737ba8f885, engine cf636b1dfb), Dart 3.13.7, package:ffi 2.2.0, Impeller-GLES
notes: Flutter Dart-AOT release, Linux GTK3 embedder, renderer: Impeller (OpenGL ES backend, default), GL = Mesa (llvmpipe under Xvfb). frame_ms = interval between consecutive FrameTiming rasterFinish timestamps (SchedulerBinding.addTimingsCallback; raster thread finished the frame and handed it to the GTK GL compositor; latest public post-render signal, not an X11 present timestamp). Only frames the engine rasterized are counted (Flutter produces no frame when nothing is dirty; every animated frame changes content). Pacing (BENCH_PACING, requested=60): native Flutter cadence = Ticker/SchedulerBinding frames driven by the engine vsync; the Linux GTK embedder registers no vsync callback, so the engine uses its fallback vsync waiter with a fixed 1/60 s tick (engine source shell/common/vsync_waiter_fallback.cc). No public/documented API uncaps it, so uncapped -> pacing "60-only". gc = null: Dart exposes no GC counters in AOT release. Warm-up 2 s; script time frozen at 0 during warm-up. images: Image(ResizeImage(FileImage, width 128, height 128)) per cell (decode at 128x128 by the engine off the UI isolate, kept in ImageCache). decode_total_ms = sum over images of wall time from first build of the cell to its first frame (file read + decode + scheduling, incl. CPU contention with llvmpipe); counters cover the whole run incl. warm-up. GridView.builder 10 columns x 128 px; scroll = triangle wave over the grid at 3000 px/s; zoom 1->3->1 over 6 s (Transform) with a sinusoidal pan; during warm-up the script is frozen at t=0.
